name: warp_register_rmsnorm_sm120
hypothesis: For row-wise RMSNorm on RTX 5060 Laptop (sm_120), keeping the sum-of-squares accumulator in registers and reducing first within warps via shuffle instructions, then across warps through a tiny shared-memory staging array, will reduce synchronization and shared-memory traffic versus a shared-memory-heavy reduction.
changes: One 256-thread block processes one contiguous row.
Use float register accumulation with fmaf for fp16, bf16, and fp32 inputs.
Use warp shuffle reduction followed by one shared array of 32 warp sums.
Use rsqrtf(mean_square + eps) and a second coalesced pass for normalization.
Compile with CUDA 13.4-compatible nvcc flags: -O3, --use_fast_math, and explicit sm_120 code generation.
constraints: No benchmark or CUDA execution was performed.
Windows-native flags only; no Linux-only compiler flags.
No affine weight or bias is applied; input shape is [rows, cols].
expected_effect: Lower reduction overhead and improved throughput for medium-to-large normalized dimensions, with the usual tradeoff that one block per row may underutilize the GPU for very short rows or very few rows.
